skill.name: connector-googledrive
skill.description: Guide Motoko Caffeine builds that connect to Google Drive through the googledrive-client and google-oauth packages.
skill.summary: Build Google Drive metadata, organization, sharing, and synchronization features with OAuth 2.0 PKCE.
skill.author: caffeinelabs

security_audit.summary: All 60 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, OAuth scope notation, and ellipsis shorthand; SKILL.md contains no executable implementation. Semantic review found dependency-installation exposure and incomplete guidance for OAuth callback binding and long-lived refresh-token protection.

remediation.issue: The installation command does not pin googledrive-client.
remediation.suggestion: Pin both mops packages to reviewed versions and document the trusted package source and upgrade review process.

remediation.issue: Refresh-token storage guidance omits confidentiality and lifecycle controls.
remediation.suggestion: Require per-user authorization, encrypted or suitably protected storage, log redaction, revocation, deletion, and upgrade-safe access controls.

remediation.issue: The OAuth callback recipe omits explicit request correlation.
remediation.suggestion: Require unpredictable state validation and bind each callback, PKCE verifier, redirect URI, and token result to the initiating user session.

content.user_title: Build Google Drive Integrations in Motoko
content.value_statement: Google Drive integrations require careful OAuth, permissions, and Internet Computer outcall configuration. This skill provides a focused Motoko recipe for metadata, organization, sharing, and synchronization.
actual_capabilities: Guides installation of the googledrive-client and google-oauth mops packages.
Describes an OAuth 2.0 PKCE authorization, exchange, and refresh flow.
Maps file, permission, comment, shared drive, revision, and change operations to client resources.
Explains why Drive outcalls must use non-replicated execution.
Shows how to configure the generated Motoko client with a bearer token.
Identifies which media upload and download operations are unsupported.
limitations: The client handles metadata but does not transfer file bytes.
Generated methods use long positional parameter lists that require consulting package signatures.
The skill does not provision Google OAuth credentials or configure a consent screen.
The skill is documentation and does not make Drive requests by itself.

use_cases.title: Create a Drive Organizer
use_cases.description: Build a Motoko service that lists, creates, renames, moves, and trashes Google Drive metadata.

use_cases.title: Add Controlled File Sharing
use_cases.description: Implement permission management with narrow OAuth scopes and explicit user authorization.

use_cases.title: Track Shared Drive Changes
use_cases.description: Design metadata synchronization using shared drives, change tokens, and non-replicated outcalls.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up the Connector
prompt_templates.prompt: Add the required Google Drive and OAuth dependencies to my Motoko project, then explain each configuration step.

prompt_templates.title: List Drive Files
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a read-only Motoko flow that authenticates a user and lists their Google Drive file metadata.

prompt_templates.title: Create and Share a Folder
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Motoko workflow that creates a Drive folder and grants one specified user access with the narrowest suitable scope.

prompt_templates.title: Design Secure Change Synchronization
prompt_templates.prompt: Architect multi-user Drive change synchronization with PKCE binding, protected refresh tokens, retries, least privilege, and non-replicated outcalls.

output_examples.input: List my Google Drive files with read-only access.
output_examples.output: A Motoko implementation plan covering OAuth consent, token exchange, client configuration, file listing, pagination, and token refresh.

output_examples.input: Create a project folder and share it with an editor.
output_examples.output: A workflow that creates folder metadata, applies an editor permission, checks each result, and avoids duplicate writes.

output_examples.input: Synchronize metadata from a shared drive.
output_examples.output: A synchronization design using shared-drive parameters, start page tokens, change pagination, retry handling, and durable checkpoints.

best_practices: Request the narrowest Google Drive scope that satisfies the user task.
Keep every Drive read and write non-replicated to prevent duplicate requests.
Protect refresh tokens and bind OAuth callbacks to the initiating user session.
anti_patterns: Do not call Google endpoints directly when the supported client covers the operation.
Do not request full Drive access for metadata-only or per-file workflows.
Do not use metadata methods for binary uploads or downloads.

faq.question: Can this connector upload file contents?
faq.answer: No. Its generated media operations are JSON typed and support metadata only.

faq.question: Which OAuth scope should I request?
faq.answer: Use drive.file when possible, then select a broader read-only scope only when required.

faq.question: Why must outcalls be non-replicated?
faq.answer: Replicated requests multiply costs and can repeat writes across subnet replicas.

faq.question: Does googledrive-client manage OAuth?
faq.answer: No. Add google-oauth separately for PKCE, authorization-code exchange, and token refresh.

faq.question: Can I use the flat API modules?
faq.answer: Yes. The flat modules remain available, while the facade stores shared configuration.

faq.question: Does this skill execute Google Drive operations?
faq.answer: No. It guides code generation and integration; the resulting application performs authorized requests.
